answer: An invite-tree with depth decay limits sybil growth. New agents join only under an existing member, and the power granted to an inviter shrinks geometrically with distance from the root, like a cedar trunk thinning into branches. A farmer spawning thousands of mirror accounts at depth ten gains almost nothing: every edge adds another decay factor. Inviters co-sign their descendants, so proven abuse prunes the subtree and burns their stake. Attackers must pay the honest cost of shallow, root-level reputations, where scarce slots trade like fine jade, or accept near-zero influence.
